title: LaBraM at Scale: Scaling Data and Models for EEG Pretraining
abstract: LaBraM, an early EEG foundation model, demonstrated that large-scale EEG pretraining can yield strong representations for diverse downstream tasks. Building on this foundation, we expand pretraining data and model capacity while retaining its core encoder and objective. We train ten encoders with 5.8 million to 1.97 billion parameters on three EEG collections spanning 25,067 to 79,910 hours, adapting signal preparation and training to heterogeneous recordings. Across 23 tasks, Atom-L* reaches 59.05% mean balanced accuracy at its best evaluated full fine-tuning (Full-FT) checkpoint, 3.61 percentage points above the strongest baseline EEG foundation model. Quark-G leads linear probing (LP) at 54.33%, a 1.24-point margin. Both also lead average task rank. At the last evaluated checkpoints, larger encoders improve Full-FT more consistently than LP, and stronger LP does not guarantee stronger Full-FT. Preserving patch structure improves LP over average pooling. Data-fraction experiments suggest capacity-dependent saturation, while checkpoint trajectories show that downstream performance can decline as pretraining loss falls. Joint classification with a shared Qwen3 readout reaches 50.50% with Molecule-H and Qwen3-8B; increasing language-model size provides no consistent gain. These results demonstrate the value of scaling LaBraM and the importance of matching pretraining scale to downstream adaptation.

title: From Natural Language to Exact Cover: A Neuro-Symbolic Approach to Zebra Puzzles
abstract: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) generation has substantially improved the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) on complex reasoning tasks, including code generation, data analysis, and exam-style question answering. Despite these advances, purely neural LLMs continue to struggle with elementary logical reasoning problems and lack the determinism, soundness, and reliability characteristic of symbolic reasoning systems. Conversely, classical symbolic methods such as SAT solving and exact cover guarantee correctness and completeness, but require problems to be expressed in highly specialized formal encodings, limiting their applicability to natural language inputs. In this work, we present a synergistic neuro-symbolic framework that bridges this gap by combining neural semantic parsing with deterministic exact cover reasoning. Given a Zebra-style logic puzzle in natural language, an LLM translates entities and constraints into structured tool calls that construct an exact cover instance. A symbolic solver then computes the solution and provides feedback to iteratively refine invalid, under- or overconstrained encodings, exploiting the uniqueness property of Zebra puzzles. We conduct a comprehensive empirical evaluation across multiple parameter scales, post-training paradigms, and LLM families. The results demonstrate that our hybrid approach consistently outperforms strong plain neural baselines, including CoT prompting, as well as recent neuro-symbolic methods.

title: FineCraft: Enhancing VLA Models for Fine-Grained Manipulation
abstract: Fine-grained manipulation couples instruction grounding, local visual precision, and sustained execution. We present FineCraft, a framework that adapts pretrained models for fine-grained manipulation in the MetaFine Challenge. A task-routed mixture of policies selects independently adapted DINOv2-DiT or pretrained π_{0.5} policies through a common observation-action interface. Local visual features help identify the instructed object parts, demonstrations and expert continuations teach the required actions, and new observations guide replanning during execution. FineCraft ranks fourth with an overall score of 0.878, exceeding the published reference on all five tasks. Official results and local diagnostics characterize performance across visual perturbations, instruction changes, and multi-stage manipulation. Code is available at https://github.com/eqcy/FineCraft

title: Accelerating Discrete Diffusion Models for Combinatorial Optimization via Momentum Inference
abstract: Neural network-based Combinatorial Optimization (CO) solvers are showing increasingly convincing performances on NP-complete (NPC) problems, alleviating the need for handcrafted heuristics. These methods are usually tested on problems with very informative features, such as coordinates in the Euclidean Traveling Salesman Problem. In this paper, we introduce D2CO-M, a discrete graph denoising diffusion model that learns how to efficiently generate high-quality solutions using an original momentum-based sampling inference strategy. The dynamics of traditional score-matching denoising diffusion can be interpreted as a stochastic gradient ascent guided by the Stein score, the gradient of the log-likelihood. D2CO-M shifts from this simple gradient ascent to a momentum-based sampling strategy fitted for discrete diffusion, inspired by fast momentum-enhanced first-order methods, as exploited in the Adam optimizer. We experiment with this momentum-based variant on two NP-hard optimization problems with complex fine-grained features: random Weighted Max-2-SAT instances, and real-world Cost Function Network instances describing Computational Protein Sequence Design problems, establishing D2CO-M as a competitive and robust tool for complex, real-world combinatorial optimization.

title: DepthGraft: Structural Regularization through Hierarchical Cross-Layer KV Reconstruction
abstract: Scaling depth is a key route to stronger large language models, but Pre-LN architectures often suffer from depth-wise information dilution, limiting the effective use of deep layers. While cross-layer connectivity has proven effective at mitigating this problem, existing designs usually introduce additional computation or memory access. We revisit cross-layer KV sharing as an efficient form of such connectivity. Beyond cache compression, each KV reuse edge creates a direct gradient path from deep layers to source KV projections, turning KV sharing into an implicit structural regularizer for KV representation geometry. We provide a systematic analysis of this mechanism, showing that proper sharing topologies sharpen key retrieval directions while enriching the value content subspace, whereas existing adjacent or global-anchor designs do not fully exploit this effect. Motivated by this, we propose DepthGraft, a hierarchical KV-sharing architecture that reconstructs deep-layer KV from stride-aligned shallow-middle source pairs. DepthGraft distributes non-local gradient flow across source layers, while preserving prefill early completion and reducing KV cache by roughly one third. Experiments on dense and MoE models from 0.5B to 16B parameters show consistent downstream improvements under both GQA and MLA. Notably, on the 16B MoE model, DepthGraft achieves a 7.0% absolute improvement on MMLU-Pro, along with gains of 6.6% on CMMLU and 6.4% on C3. These results validate the potential of DepthGraft as a scalable design for large-scale pretraining. The project page is available at https://github.com/jianke0604/DepthGraft.

title: Knowledge Organization Matters: How Graph Design and Temporal Structure Shape Agentic AI Performance on Drilling Activity Reports
abstract: Abstract Agentic AI over drilling reports can automate analytics that today take hours per question, from non-productive-time trending to offset-well lookup. Published systems typically commit to a single graph design without testing it: most studies in literature perform multi-method comparisons and evaluate whole pipelines and do not evaluate individual design decisions. We compare five ways of organizing a corpus for an agent (a vectorless reasoning tree, an open-vocabulary graph, that graph with community post-processing, a domain-schema graph, and a fine-grained quantitative graph) against a shared flat-vector baseline, on two public corpora: 1,681 Daily Drilling Reports from Equinor's Volve field (North Sea, 1992–2016) and 1,888 Weekly Activity Reports from Shell Offshore operations in the Gulf of Mexico (BSEE eWell archive, 2022–2024). We benchmark a ReAct agent that runs the full matrix at four capability tiers: two successive frontier versions, a fast-tier cloud model, and an open-weights 26B model on a 16 GB consumer GPU. Under frontier agents the vectorless tree leads relevance on both corpora, while hybrid retrieval leads completeness against machine-verified answer keys, with the domain-schema hybrid the strongest graph configuration. A blinded pair-preserved scoring of all 1,080 frontier cells confirms the BSEE architecture effects: hybrid retrieval beats vector-only (+0.040, Holm-corrected p=0.0004), the schema step over the open-vocabulary control is the largest effect measured (+0.068), and community post-processing alone does not contribute anything. The architecture ranking reproduces at every capability tier, and the spread widens as the agent weakens. A bi-temporal fact table with a point-in-time query tool raises as-of accuracy to 1.00 on both corpora, correcting all nine static errors with no regressions (96 paired queries, exact McNemar p=0.004). A schema audit shows the cost of a hand-designed ontology: named storms present in 30 reports were invisible to schema-graph retrieval, producing confident false negatives that open-vocabulary and vector retrieval avoided.

title: Pretraining Data Scale Reverses the Muon-AdamW Fine-Tuning Gap
abstract: Muon has recently emerged as a promising optimizer for pretraining large language models, offering a speedup over AdamW in minimizing pretraining loss. However, it remains unclear whether Muon's advantage persists after fine-tuning. In this paper, we study the downstream behavior of Muon and AdamW and uncover a surprising trend: beyond a sufficiently large pretraining data budget, AdamW outperforms Muon after fine-tuning. Moreover, as model size increases, AdamW overtakes Muon at progressively smaller pretraining token-parameter ratios. To explain this reversal, we view fine-tuning as a perturbation of the outputs and introduce the margin-to-spread ratio, which measures how far the correct logit lies above the wrong ones relative to how widely the wrong logits are spread. In language models, Muon has the larger margin-to-spread ratio at small data budgets and AdamW at large ones, mirroring the fine-tuning trend. In a linear associative memory, we prove that after one update the margin-to-spread ratio of gradient descent gains on that of Muon as the data budget grows, and simulations show that this trend persists after extended training.

evidence.abstract: Muon has recently emerged as a promising optimizer for pretraining large language models, offering a speedup over AdamW in minimizing pretraining loss. However, it remains unclear whether Muon's advantage persists after fine-tuning. In this paper, we study the downstream behavior of Muon and AdamW and uncover a surprising trend: beyond a sufficiently large pretraining data budget, AdamW outperforms Muon after fine-tuning. Moreover, as model size increases, AdamW overtakes Muon at progressively smaller pretraining token-parameter ratios. To explain this reversal, we view fine-tuning as a perturbation of the outputs and introduce the margin-to-spread ratio, which measures how far the correct logit lies above the wrong ones relative to how widely the wrong logits are spread. In language models, Muon has the larger margin-to-spread ratio at small data budgets and AdamW at large ones, mirroring the fine-tuning trend. In a linear associative memory, we prove that after one update the margin-to-spread ratio of gradient descent gains on that of Muon as the data budget grows, and simulations show that this trend persists after extended training.

title: DR Pixel: Page-Native Deep Research with Vision-Language Models
abstract: Complex documents such as scientific papers contain rich information in tables, figures, and equations; however, existing deep research (DR) agents typically reduce papers to OCR-extracted text. We instead ask whether vision-language models (VLMs) can enable page-native deep research: directly retrieving and reasoning over rendered document page images. We introduce DR Pixel, the first open-source end-to-end multimodal DR agent that uses rendered page images as its sole retrieval and reasoning unit, operating over a corpus of 1.06M pages. To evaluate this setting, we construct DRPixelBench, a benchmark on scientific papers requiring reasoning over text, figures, tables, and equations. Surprisingly, page-native DR already works well without training, outperforming OCR-based baselines across state-of-the-art models like GPT-5.4, Gemini-3.5-Flash, and Qwen3.6-27B, while requiring fewer tool calls. We next turn to DR training. A key challenge is that teacher trajectories for agentic supervised finetuning are noisy, mixing critical reasoning and action steps with redundant or failed attempts. To address this, we introduce counterfactual credit reweighting, a fine-grained credit assignment method that weights individual reasoning and action steps by their counterfactual contribution to the final answer. Our training improves retrieval recall by about 15 points and final accuracy by over 10 points on DRPixelBench, and likewise outperforms the untrained baseline on four existing benchmarks. On out-of-distribution ViDoRe-V3, DR Pixel comes within 1.8 points of an oracle that is given the gold pages directly. Our results suggest that the conventional OCR-then-retrieve pipeline is not only unnecessary but suboptimal: directly retrieving and reasoning over visual document pages makes complex DR both more effective and more efficient.

title: Explainable Financial Fraud Detection Using Graph Neural Networks: A Comparative Study
abstract: Abstract The financial fraud detection problem is extremely complicated and difficult because of the relationships between transactions in financial systems and the extreme imbalance of fraudulent and legitimate transactions. Traditional machine learning methods might not be suitable for modeling the relational nature of transaction networks, which is the reason why graph neural networks (GNNs) are employed in graph-based fraud detection. This research evaluates the performance of three different GNN architectures: Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN), GraphSAGE, and Graph Attention Networks (GAT) in the field of financial fraud detection using Elliptic's Bitcoin transaction dataset. The dataset is a temporal graph of bitcoin transactions, allowing to analyze transaction attributes and relationships. The study creates a comparative experimental setup for testing the three architectures according to classification metrics, focusing on the precision, recall and F1 score of fraud-class accuracy together with overall accuracy. The interpretability problem of graph-based predictions is overcome by plugging GNNExplainer into a unified explanation pipeline to locate the structure of subgraphs and the features of nodes that are relevant to each prediction from the model. This framework brings together prediction, explanation, and visualization at the instance level, to facilitate a discussion of model performance and interpretability. The goals of the study are to describe the strengths and weaknesses of the architectures evaluated and to evaluate the usefulness of graph-based explanations for financial fraud detection. Experimental conclusions will be verified based on the results of the model and explanation analyses.

title: Not All Reasoning Generalizes: A Case Study on Learning Generalizable Reasoning Strategies in RLVR
abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) can enable generalizable improvement for large language model (LLM) reasoning. This paper studies how to incentivize such generalization via reasoning strategies. We study this question with a controllable equation-solving framework: finding multiple inputs x for equations f(x)=y, where f is a non-bijective string function. This setting makes reasoning strategies observable while supporting a clear definition of easy-to-hard out-of-distribution (OOD) shifts, e.g., more solutions, longer y, etc. We uncover a subtle RLVR failure: it teaches the model to solve in-distribution tasks with high accuracy and structured step-by-step derivation, yet under OOD shifts, the same model abandons derivation and collapses to ineffective brute-force enumeration, causing sharp accuracy drops. This observation reveals the deeper challenges of RLVR generalization as it is neither incapable base model nor reward hacking, since the model succeeds in-distribution with the correct reasoning strategy. The key to mitigating this failure is an indirect intervention that surprisingly helps: co-training with bijective inversion tasks. Although these bijective tasks are actually not uniformly harder and even further from the non-bijective OOD evaluation, they make derivation more certain and substantially restore the correct strategy and accuracy under OOD shifts. This effect further motivates our theoretical analysis: outcome-only RLVR can shape reasoning processes through implicitly crediting the effective reasoning strategies more, even without process supervision. To conclude, our analysis framework and findings systematically reveal the crucial role and incentivization of reasoning strategies in RLVR generalization under OOD shifts. Code is available at https://github.com/ziqipang/rl_meta_thinking.

title: Avatar Intelligence: Amplifying Human Agency Through Persistent Personal Agents
abstract: Personal AI agents are increasingly capable of handling long-horizon tasks across applications, yet users often need to invest substantial effort in specifying goals, resolving ambiguity, and verifying outcomes. We argue that progress should be measured by how effectively agents amplify human agency: enabling people to pursue their goals with less routine supervision while retaining control over consequential decisions. We advocate Avatar Intelligence, a paradigm of persistent personal agents that represent users' goals, values, and constraints through sustained decision delegation across contexts and time. We describe a maturity roadmap from human-directed execution to autonomous operation within delegated domains, and introduce the Agentic Oversight Index (AOI) as a framework for evaluating delivered value against agent-side operational cost and human oversight burden. We identify three core research challenges: identity-continuous personalization that carries user preferences across tasks, user-situated evolution through Rehearsal Engineering, and safety mechanisms that combine technical control with accountability and recourse. These directions define a research agenda for reliable decision delegation to personal agents across tasks and over time.

title: FLAMIA: FLAsh MIcroscaling Attention for Fast and Causally Safe Training on Blackwell
abstract: Attention remains a substantial computational cost in Transformer training, particularly at long context lengths. NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs provide high-throughput low-precision matrix multiplication, but exploiting it in attention requires addressing quantization overhead, causal information leakage through shared scales, and numerical inconsistencies between the forward and backward passes. We present FLAMIA, a family of attention kernels for Blackwell with MXFP8 and mixed NVFP4/FP8 training paths. Our design combines token-block scaling that reuses quantized operands across matrix orientations, targeted safeguards against scale-induced leakage, and consistent forward and backward computations. Fused quantization and architecture-specific kernel optimizations reduce overhead, while document-local scaling and workload-aware scheduling support variable-length documents directly in packed layouts without repacking. Across various causal packed-document workloads, the MXFP8 path accelerates the combined forward and backward attention call, including quantization, by factors of $1.10$--$1.40\times$ on B200 and $1.06$--$1.42\times$ on B300 relative to the fastest evaluated baseline for each workload. We validate training stability and quality preservation on pretraining Llama-style models. These results show how jointly designing quantization, training numerics, and document scheduling translates low-bit hardware throughput into practical attention acceleration.

title: Sentiment Analysis and Topic Modelling of Public Opinion on TikTok Regarding Palm Oil Plantation Expansion in Papua
abstract: Palm oil plantation expansion in Papua has triggered diverse public responses on TikTok. This study analyzes public sentiment and identifies discussion topics regarding this policy using a deep learning approach. Data comprises 3,999 comments collected from the official Kumparan news account concerning President Prabowo Subianto's speech on Papuan land opening. We utilized IndoBERT for sentiment analysis and BERTopic for topic modeling. The results indicate that negative sentiment predominates (39.31%), followed by neutral (38.51%) and positive (22.18%) sentiments. This negativity stems primarily from ecological concerns, specifically flood risks and deforestation, alongside economic stability issues. Furthermore, topic modeling reveals four primary themes: Political Actors, Environmental Issues, Economic Issues, and Emotional-Spiritual Reactions. The study highlights a disconnect between government development goals and public fears concerning environmental risks and household welfare. As a practical implication, these findings provide a direct empirical basis for policymakers. The government must prioritize ecological mitigation and economic stability measures when designing sustainable development strategies in Papua to effectively address digital public concerns.

title: Isekai3D SDG: A Platform for Diverse Synthetic Gameplay Visual Data
abstract: We present Isekai3D Synthetic Data Generation (SDG), a platform for simulating and capturing synthetic 3D gameplay for research in vision and world models, neural graphics, gameplay agents, and other applications. The platform combines reusable environment and character assets with Unreal Engine plugins in a two-stage workflow. First, world simulation generates gameplay while recording the world state, character movements, actions, and camera tracks needed for replay. Second, the recorded simulation is replayed to capture selected outputs, such as rendered video, images, and depth maps, at a specified resolution and frame rate under selected rendering and camera configurations. Separating simulation from capture allows the same recorded gameplay to produce multiple output variants without repeating the original simulation. Visual outputs are accompanied by frame-aligned camera, character, and action metadata. The platform uploads generated data directly in a training-friendly format, reducing intermediate storage, preparation time, and manual processing. This report describes the design of our overall system, including the platform's assets, plugins, and their functionality, explaining how they work together to generate diverse synthetic gameplay data.

title: VLM-as-a-Judge for Person Re-Identification
abstract: Cloth-changing person re-identification (CC-ReID) is still very challenging, and no method clearly dominates: methods that lead on one benchmark collapse on the others, because they rest on different identity cues. We show that a general-purpose vision-language model (VLM), used zero-shot as a judge for reranking a short candidate list, beats the expert retrieval models it reranks by a wide and consistent margin. On the four scenarios of CHIRLA, a long-term CC-ReID benchmark that no publicly released Re-ID model is trained on, reranking the candidates of two frozen experts raises rank-1 on every scenario, by 12.9 points on average over the best expert and 9.4 over the best naive ensemble of the two, with no component fine-tuned on the target data. Merging both experts' shortlists matches or beats reranking the stronger expert's shortlist alone, at lower cost. Introducing a VLM does, however, come at a cost: almost all of the pipeline's FLOPs are spent on it. We therefore borrow a criterion from ensembling and invoke the VLM judge only where the two experts disagree at rank 1. This threshold-free gate removes 40% of the calls, and a comparable share of total compute, with no significant drop in rank-1, trading 1.8 to 3.8 points of mAP. Judging remains the dominant cost, but on a benchmark where dedicated experts stall, we find a frozen general-purpose model to be the strongest judge of identity. The code is available at https://github.com/bdager/JudgeReID.

title: When is a Density Rule Enough? a Field Benchmark of Anomaly Detectors for Real-Time Mud Monitoring
abstract: Abstract Real-time drilling fluid monitoring systems stream continuous multivariate mud measurements at sub-minute cadence, and the volume of data exceeds what screen watching can absorb. A practical question follows for any deployment: is a simple statistical rule on density sufficient, or is multivariate machine learning needed? This study benchmarks four anomaly detectors on a 48-hour online drilling fluid monitoring field record, with mud density as the primary trigger and temperature, water fraction, oil fraction, solids content, and plastic viscosity as contextual channels. The detectors are a calibrated 1) Shewhart and CUSUM rule on density, 2) a two-window multivariate change-point test, 3) an isolation forest, and 4) a one-class support vector machine. All detectors train unsupervised per continuous segment without event labels, and every threshold is set on a held-out early slice of the same segment so that all four alarm at the same rate during normal operation. Performance is quantified by event-level recall and precision, first-flag latency, false-alarm clusters per hour, and single-core runtime. The record contains three density collapse events with a common oil-phase dilution signature; density, water fraction, solids content, and plastic viscosity fall while oil fraction rises, with temperature falling in two events and rising in one. All four detectors recover all three events. The density rule flags the sharp events at onset but is 139 seconds late on the gradual event, whose onset is led by a decline in plastic viscosity and which the multivariate detectors flag at or before onset. At equal recall, the one-class SVM and the change-point test roughly halve the false-alarm rate of the density rule (0.68 and 0.72 against 1.28 clusters per hour), while the isolation forest matches the density rule when its threshold is frozen on the early slice. Requiring multivariate confirmation of density-rule alerts removes 14 to 21 of 25 false alarms. All detectors run within 0.001 to 0.09 ms per record on a single core. A detector selection framework based on the kind of events expected, the tolerable false-alarm rate, and sensor availability is provided.

title: FADE: Factored Ability--Difficulty Filtering for Online RLVR Scheduling
abstract: Group-based reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) learns only from prompts whose sampled completions disagree: all-pass and all-fail groups produce zero relative advantage and burn generation budget without moving the policy. Adaptive schedulers try to steer rollouts toward informative prompts, yet they rely on per-prompt pass-rate trackers that entangle two quantities evolving at very different speeds---the policy's shifting competence across reasoning skills and each prompt's intrinsic difficulty. When a single exponential average or Beta counter tracks both at once, short memory scrambles the relative ordering of prompts whereas long memory reports stale pass rates. We introduce FADE (Factored Ability--Difficulty Estimation), a bilinear state-space filter that separates the two timescales. FADE represents each prompt's success logit as the inner product of a whitened $K$-dimensional skill loading with a fast-drifting policy ability vector, minus a slow-shrinking scalar item intercept. Using Pólya--Gamma augmentation, each minibatch of binary rollout outcomes updates the $K$-dimensional ability posterior in closed form via a rank-$K$ Woodbury step, instantly transferring competence shifts to all unobserved prompts that share those skills while leaving item intercepts stable. From the resulting posterior mean and variance we derive a closed-form utility for the probability of drawing a non-degenerate rollout group. Across five reasoning benchmarks, two base models, and four scheduling paradigms under a matched rollout budget, FADE consistently improves downstream accuracy and calibration while adding less than $0.6$\,ms per step.

title: Can You Predict the Next Mind? Toward Multi-Turn Multi-Party Mental World Modeling
abstract: While multimodal foundation models have achieved remarkable progress in physical world modeling, generation, and embodied reasoning, their capacity for dynamic mental world modeling remains underexplored. Existing benchmarks predominantly focus on static mental state perception or short-horizon decision-making, overlooking the dynamic mental trajectories inherent in multi-party, multi-turn interactions. To bridge this gap, we introduce M^3WME-Bench, a benchmark designed to evaluate mental world modeling conditioned on the evolving actions of interactants. Specifically, models are tasked with forecasting a target subject's future mental states and behaviors over extended social interactions. In addition to the benchmark suite, we construct M^3WME-23K, a dedicated training dataset, and establish a competitive baseline named MindNext-7B. Extensive evaluations across four representative paradigms (general MLLMs, emotion-specialized MLLMs, agentic frameworks, and World Foundation Models) reveal that current systems consistently struggle to anticipate forward-looking mental states. Mechanistic analyses further reveal that existing architectures fundamentally lack forward mental state transition dynamics. Our findings highlight a pivotal challenge in advancing agents from physical to mental world modeling, charting new directions for socially adaptive AI.

evidence.title: Can You Predict the Next Mind? Toward Multi-Turn Multi-Party Mental World Modeling
evidence.abstract: While multimodal foundation models have achieved remarkable progress in physical world modeling, generation, and embodied reasoning, their capacity for dynamic mental world modeling remains underexplored. Existing benchmarks predominantly focus on static mental state perception or short-horizon decision-making, overlooking the dynamic mental trajectories inherent in multi-party, multi-turn interactions. To bridge this gap, we introduce M^3WME-Bench, a benchmark designed to evaluate mental world modeling conditioned on the evolving actions of interactants. Specifically, models are tasked with forecasting a target subject's future mental states and behaviors over extended social interactions. In addition to the benchmark suite, we construct M^3WME-23K, a dedicated training dataset, and establish a competitive baseline named MindNext-7B. Extensive evaluations across four representative paradigms (general MLLMs, emotion-specialized MLLMs, agentic frameworks, and World Foundation Models) reveal that current systems consistently struggle to anticipate forward-looking mental states. Mechanistic analyses further reveal that existing architectures fundamentally lack forward mental state transition dynamics. Our findings highlight a pivotal challenge in advancing agents from physical to mental world modeling, charting new directions for socially adaptive AI.

title: vir: a Verification IR measured in two logics (Lean 4 and MetaPRL)
abstract: One frozen object, the appendix of the O94 paper on verification agents, mechanised in Lean 4 and in MetaPRL's Computational Type Theory against predictions committed before either arm's first proof, with a harness that re-derives every count from the artifacts. Its first application is a compiler: the appendix's lowering to x86-64 joined to the specification over x86lean.

title: Thought-deciphering via hierarchical EEG-to-text alignment
abstract: Communication is important for our well-being, but it can be impaired by disabilities, such as locked-in syndrome (LIS), cerebral palsy (CP), and dysarthria. Non-invasive brain-to-text brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) offer a promising solution by providing an alternative communication pathway for people with communication disabilities. However, most recent breakthroughs have relied on large, cumbersome, and costly neuroimaging modalities, such as functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and magnetoencephalography (MEG). Numerous studies have attempted decoding using the lighter and cheaper electroencephalography (EEG), but the results remain inferior compared to the other modalities. More importantly, we do not understand how these modalities are related to text at the letter, word, sentence, and higher semantic levels. Many prior studies have focused on decoding below the sentence level because it is considerably easier to design an experiment around phonemes, letters, and words. However, during communication, sentences play a much more important role than words and letters. This is because sentences carry information at such a high level that they can be understood even if some words and letters are missing. However, within sentence-level decoding, sentence classification is not as well investigated as sentence generation, making it difficult to decide whether a sentence should be retrieved or generated in the context of EEG-to-text decoding. This paper strives to investigate sentence-level EEG-to-text classification via a novel hierarchical alignment framework, where the main goal is to retrieve a read sentence using its context and EEG as inputs.

title: PhotoGuider: Composition-Aware Cropping and 360^{circ} View Framing with Explainable Photographic Assessments
abstract: Traditional image cropping assumes the photograph already contains the composition worth keeping, and asks only where to crop. A full 360^{circ} scene offers no such guarantee: the viewing direction in a scene has to be discovered before anything can be framed. We present PhotoGuider, a measure-then-frame method that answers both questions with compact learned scorers over one shared set of composition-aware features. The designed features are extracted using foundation and task-specific vision models and structured into four photographic tokens: Subject, Composition, Aesthetics, and Integrity. Our MLLM explainer is fine-tuned to generate composition-related explanations conditioned on images and measured token assessments. To our knowledge, PhotoGuider is the first method to combine explicit composition-based direction selection in 360^{circ} panoramas with refined framing, camera-parameter output for native re-rendering, and measurement-conditioned explanations. On two standard 2D cropping benchmarks, PhotoGuider achieves the highest average mIoU performance against ground-truth crops. In a blind ranking study, 120 participants ranked three cropping methods over 100 panoramic scenes from the public Poly Haven HDRI library, placing our framings first in 53.2% of cases, against 27.3% and 19.5% for two strong alternatives. Project page: https://ntuneillee.github.io/research/photoguider/

title: IdeaTaste: Do LLMs Share the Research Taste of Human Researchers?
abstract: Research taste, the judgment of what to read, which problems to pursue, and which methods to try, increasingly shapes the work of AI scientists, yet it remains far less understood than their ability to execute research. We introduce IdeaTaste, a benchmark that scores an LLM by how closely the research proposals it writes from a literature snapshot frozen at 2025 match the work the same communities published in 2026. Our experiments span six contemporary language models and four research areas from established to emerging fields, covering more than 90{,}000 proposals in total. LLM agents fall well short of human communities in both the literature they cite and the ideas they state, reaching about 26\% of the human level on citation matching and only 18\% on idea matching. Their populations can cite as diversely as a community and take up its tasks and methods, yet rarely arrive at the concrete approaches and research plans it pursues. Neither richer field context nor larger populations substantially close this gap. In blinded expert review, AI proposals trail the 2026 papers least in presentation and most in expected success, echoing their gap in concrete approaches, and those whose ideas no human paper shares fare worst, suggesting weaker directions rather than overlooked opportunities. These results indicate that the main bottleneck in AI research taste lies less in finding the directions a community works on than in turning them into the concrete approaches it goes on to pursue. We release IdeaTaste as an open, continuously updated leaderboard (https://cxcscmu.github.io/IdeaTaste) that benchmarks contemporary AI proposals against future publication cycles.

title: Interdisciplinary Agentic AI Deployment: A Success Story from the Malay Basin, Malaysia
abstract: Subsurface professionals working in the oil and gas exploration and production industry are routinely exposed to a wide and diverse array of specialized software packages, digital tools, and sophisticated applications. These have been developed by various international technology companies, service organizations, and independent software vendors from around the world to help geoscientists, engineers, and technical analysts conduct their complex geological studies, detailed reservoir interpretations, and comprehensive data analysis tasks with greater efficiency and accuracy. The selection of one particular software solution over another competing alternative in the marketplace is primarily driven by several key factors. These include the software's comprehensive technical capabilities, its specific functional features, and perhaps most importantly, the individual user's personal proficiency, accumulated hands-on experience, and overall comfort level with the tool developed over months or years of regular use. When the technical capabilities and available features appear to be roughly equivalent or comparable between different software options, professionals naturally and instinctively gravitate toward the software platform with which they are most familiar and have the greatest operational experience using in their daily work activities. This well-established and understandable preference for familiar and well-understood tools, however, inevitably introduces significant operational friction across different workflows. This is particularly problematic when technical teams need to transition between various disconnected tools from different software vendors, which frequently results in operational delays, increased inefficiencies, potential data loss or corruption, and considerable frustration among team members who must constantly adapt to new interfaces and workflows.

title: SpecOPD: Branch-Parallel On-Policy Distillation for Speculative Decoding
abstract: Speculative decoding (SD) accelerates large language model inference by reducing the sequential cost of token-by-token generation. Advanced SD methods reduce proposal cost with parallel drafters that predict entire blocks in one forward pass, but overall speedup still depends on acceptance length. On-policy distillation (OPD) can push well-trained drafters beyond acceptance-length plateaus, yet conventional pipelines collect supervision through sequential draft-and-verify rollouts. Our key insight is that on-policy supervision need not inherit these dependencies: a draft block can be supervised using only its reference prefix and draft-sampled history. We propose SpecOPD, a branch-parallel OPD framework that parallelizes draft sampling and target supervision across independent branches drawn from the evolving drafter policy at reference anchors. We pack these branches into proposal trees to share target-prefix computation, using tree masks for full attention, branch-consistent indexer groups for sparse attention, and indexed state replay for linear attention to preserve each branch's history. We train the drafter with an E2E-TV surrogate that directly targets acceptance length. Our study spans 8B full-attention (GQA), 27B full-linear (GQA--GDN), and 125B sparse-linear (QSA--GDN) targets, three parallel draft architectures (DFlash, DSpark, and DFlash V2), and four task domains (dialogue, coding, mathematics, and agentic). SpecOPD achieves up to 41.45% higher mean acceptance length, 16.09times supervised-token throughput over sequential-rollout OPD under native configurations, and up to 3.56times generation speedup over autoregressive decoding.

title: Strategist: Evolving Reasoning with Agents
abstract: A model is only half of an AI agent system. The other half is the inference strategy: the reasoning procedure that turns model calls into a response. Today that second half is written by hand, and the experience of building one strategy never carries to the next. We introduce Strategist, a meta-agent that evolves inference strategies across tasks. Each strategy is written as a blueprint,executable code that other strategies can reuse, and together the blueprints form a library. Given a task and a small development set, Strategist retrieves related blueprints, writes candidate strategies, tests them on real samples, and revises them from the results. Every candidate then enters the library, so later tasks build on earlier discoveries. On 30 benchmarks, Strategist beats the strongest baseline on 24 and matches its average accuracy (74.7% vs.74.0%) at 39% lower inference cost. Its strategies also transfer to unseen tasks and other models without further search. The part of an AI system that is not improved on its own now does.

title: Reimagining computational quantum research with AI scientists
abstract: AI scientists are expanding automated research across scientific domains, yet their ability to turn the scientific record into a foundation for autonomous discovery remains elusive. Here we uncover a fundamental barrier to this transition and demonstrate a route to overcome it in computational quantum science, where advances shape both what we can learn from complex quantum systems and what quantum computing can ultimately deliver. To identify this barrier, we introduce OmniQ, an expert-audited virtual research environment that converts published studies into executable reproduction tasks. Across 59 papers spanning classical simulation, quantum algorithms and quantum-property characterization, we systematically evaluate five agentic systems powered by large language models and six third-party agent harnesses. Our findings reveal that current AI scientists often fail to reproduce published results, exposing a fundamental mismatch between what scientific papers communicate and what autonomous agents require. By contrast, human expert intervention can turn these failures into successful reproductions, showing that the missing information can be identified and converted into reusable research experience. Guided by this observation, we develop Residual Agents (RA), a quantum-tailored self-improving AI scientist that distils externally verified workflow repairs into such experience. RA substantially improves research performance under fixed base models and limited adaptation budgets. For example, RA raises DeepSeek V4.1 Flash performance from 68% to 85%, matching Claude Code with Opus 5 at a third of its cost despite using a weaker base model. We integrate all reproduced results into an extensible platform built on the model context protocol, making verified research workflows directly accessible to AI scientists and allowing new scientific papers to be continuously incorporated.

title: Beyond Binary: Harmonizing Wave Hardware and Quantum Biophysics Through Exact Linear-Time Computing Over Discrete Dielectric Lattices
abstract: Beyond Binary: How Single-Transit Photonic Resonance and Dynamic Quantum Biophysics Solves the Decoherence Barrier ABSTRACT This work synthesizes a fundamental paradigm shift in computational physics and hardware architecture, uniting non-binary photonic wave interference with lossless, open-system quantum dynamics. Traditional computational paradigms suffer from two foundational bottlenecks: binary CMOS architecture bound by Landauer switching heat and von Neumann memory bus latency, and quantum simulations constrained by exponential Hilbert-space state blowup and environmental decoherence. Here, we establish the mathematical and physical foundations of Discrete Lattice Resonance Architecture (DLRA) operating alongside the Classical Quantum Biophysics (CQBP) simulation framework. 1. Photonic Substrate and Non-Binary Instruction Set We present a fixed-topology, single-transit optical core inscribed within an \\(\alpha\\)-quartz dielectric lattice containing core-shell Schottky junction nodes. Logic execution shifts from binary (1/0) gate switching to the continuous Octad Instruction Tuple \\(\Theta = (A, \phi_1, \phi_2, \phi_3, \phi_4, \sigma, \chi, \omega)\\), parameterizing pulse amplitude, quadrant phases, duration, polarization, and spatial carrier frequencies. Global matrix-vector transformations (\\(10^{12}\\) MACs/transit) execute within a single 21-picosecond optical transit (\\(\tau \approx 21\text{ ps}\\)), eliminating transistor gate-switching heat and memory bus delays entirely. 2. Diffeomorphic Reduction and State-Space Linearization We formalize the mathematical reduction of non-linear system flows and infinite-dimensional differential operators into exact, finite matrix updates. By establishing Lie algebra intertwining conditions over generator-closed invariant carriers, complex non-linear dynamics—including post-quantum cryptographic trapdoors (such as AES-128 key recovery)—are mapped via pullback transformations into exact linear-time (\\(\mathcal{O}(N)\\)) matrix-vector evolutions, resolving classical state-space search explosions. 3. Dynamically Coupled Open-System Quantum Biophysics To bridge classical molecular mechanics with open quantum systems, the CQBP engine introduces an object-oriented hierarchy inheriting from a unified `Simulator` base class. Classical particle dynamics (`MolecularDynamics`), driven by velocity Verlet integration of Lennard-Jones pair potentials with center-of-mass motion removal, operate in direct lockstep with open density matrix evolutions (`QuantumDynamics`): Dynamic Lindblad Coupling: Classical interatomic strain \\(r(t)\\) dynamically parameterizes the non-autonomous Lindblad superoperator \\(\mathcal{L}_t\\), modulating instantaneous dephasing rates \\(\gamma(t) = \max\left(\gamma_{\text{min}}, \gamma_0 \left[1 + \eta \left(\frac{r(t)-r_0}{r_0}\right)\right]\right)\\) and jump operators. Strict Conservation Laws: Fourth-order Runge-Kutta (RK4) and exact matrix exponential solvers explicitly enforce matrix Hermiticity \\(0.5(\rho + \rho^\dagger)\\) and unit trace normalization \\(\text{Tr}(\rho) = 1.0\\) at every integration step, preventing unphysical probability leakage or floating-point norm drift. Entropy Generation Kinetics: Real-time diagnostic observers measure quantum state populations \\(\rho_{ii}\\), off-diagonal coherences \\(\rho_{ij}\\), state purity \\(\text{Tr}(\rho^2)\\), and von Neumann entropy \\(S = -\text{Tr}(\rho \ln \rho)\\) with numerical zero-eigenvalue filtering (\\(\lambda > 10^{-10}\\)). Path Integral Discretization: Quantum statistical mechanics and zero-point thermal delocalization (mean radius of gyration \\(R_g = 0.0524\text{ nm}\\) at \\(T = 300\text{ K}\\)) are computed deterministically via ring-polymer bead chains (`PathIntegral`). 4. Quantitative Benchmarks & Physical Analysis Validation across a \\(3.0\text{ ps}\\) trajectory under a \\(1.5\text{ THz}\\) vibrational drive demonstrates real-time vibrational sideband imprinting onto off-diagonal quantum coherences \\(|\rho_{01}(t)|\\), thermal equilibration at \\(101.30\text{ K}\\), population relaxation to ground state \\(\rho_{00} = 0.5263\\) and excited state \\(\rho_{11} = 0.4737\\), and monotonic entropy stabilization at \\(S = 0.5789\\) with zero trace drift (\\(\text{Error} < 10^{-16}\\)). By uniting single-transit wave-interference hardware with zero-drift open quantum software, this framework replaces continuous differential singularities with exact discrete algebra, providing an exascale computational foundation for room-temperature quantum biology, bio-photonic engineering, and hardware security. title: Tracing the Scientific Discovery Capacity of LLMs to Their Training Data
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) show growing promise for scientific discovery, yet basic questions remain about what enables reliable discovery. How can we trace the scientific discovery capacity of LLMs to their training data? We study this question as one of missing probability mass and develop a theoretical account in which monofacts-the facts observed once during training-set the discovery capacity. In materials science and regulatory genomics, we directly manipulate monofact rates in training sets and find that more monofacts consistently yield more discoveries across two open-weight model families, sampling strategies, and reasoning budgets. Further experiments show the relationship cannot be explained by training-set diversity alone and can transfer across scientific domains when paired with in-domain data. Together, our results identify monofact rate in training data as a key factor governing discoveries in language models.

title: RxnMiner: A Multimodal Agent for Structured Reaction Data Extraction from Chemistry Figures
abstract: Reaction data underpin machine learning for reaction prediction, condition recommendation, and retrosynthetic planning, yet extracting these data from literature figures still requires substantial manual effort. Many figures encode multiple experiments through shared templates, substituent tables, and product grids. Recovering concrete reaction records therefore requires molecular recognition, association of evidence with individual experimental entries, and reconstruction of indirectly specified participants. We present RxnMiner, a multimodal agent system that combines an expert-informed extraction procedure with a chemistry toolbox to coordinate these operations. The agent reads molecular structures, resolves shared and entry-specific evidence, and instantiates participants from templates to assemble source-linked reaction records. We also introduce ChemRxn-Bench, a benchmark of 603 reaction figures with 8,547 manually annotated and reviewed reaction records, evaluated under a common protocol for exact molecular identity and reactant-product pairing. On this benchmark, with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next as the backbone, RxnMiner raises stereochemistry-aware reaction macro-F1 from 21.0% under direct prediction to 71.0%, compared with 25.0% for the strongest existing extraction system. Across five backbones, it also outperforms the same base agent without the extraction procedure and chemistry toolbox by 9.4 to 25.5 points. Applied without human intervention to 10,107 literature figures, RxnMiner produces a silver corpus of 88,202 source-linked reaction records.

title: VidDub: Replacement-Aware Distillation for Two-Step Video Dubbing
abstract: Video dubbing aims to synthesize lip movements that match target speech while preserving the speaker identity, head pose, and background of a source video. Existing editors are predominantly trained via self-reconstruction under original paired audio, even though the source mouth becomes a conflicting target when driving speech is replaced. We introduce replacement-aware cross-audio supervision: paired-audio samples use full-frame reconstruction, whereas unpaired replacement-audio samples mask out source-mouth reconstruction losses and supervise the mouth solely through audio-visual synchronization while preserving unmasked facial regions and background. Because offline dubbing provides the complete source video and target speech beforehand, we present VidDub, a full-context diffusion editor distilled into two denoising steps (2 NFE). Our replacement-aware teacher first learns accurate lip synchronization without regressing toward conflicting source mouth movements. Matched trajectory regression then transfers the teacher's CFG-guided trajectories to a two-step student, and distribution matching distillation recovers visual quality after step compression. We will release the curated training dataset, VidDub-Bench, fixed paired- and cross-audio evaluation manifests, preprocessing outputs, and unified evaluation code. Across three training seeds, masking out conflicting source-mouth reconstruction improves cross-audio Sync-C by 0.833; the final two-step model combines strong lip synchronization with superior visual quality, identity preservation, and visual speech recognition across four benchmarks.

title: TaoMate-HD: Progressive-Resolution Autoregressive Audio-Video Generation
abstract: Streaming digital humans produce detailed video while continuing speech as new text arrives. High-resolution denoising is costly, and text updates can cause repeated or interrupted speech. We present TaoMate-HD, an autoregressive model for high-resolution audio-video streaming. For each short segment, or chunk, two denoising steps establish coarse video structure at low resolution. A final step refines the video to high resolution, with audio generated throughout the same trajectory. Each stage passes its audiovisual predictions to the same stage of the next chunk as history. Across text updates, the model retains this history to infer what has already been spoken. Continuation training utilizes asymmetric text conditioning, with separate text windows for generation and distillation. Experiments show a 1.6x speedup over direct high-resolution generation with the same model and hardware. Optimized stage-parallel deployment provides a further 1.9x overall speedup over serial progressive generation. Our continuation training reduces character error rate by 11.18 percentage points relative to the baseline. The model also supports hour-long audiovisual generation. Our project page is https://taoliveaigc.github.io/TaoMate-HD.

title: Bounded Autonomy: A Budget-Constrained Framework for AI Agent Operations Toward Safety-Critical Process Environments
abstract: Abstract Tight autonomy budgets improve safety for AI agents in process control with bounded completion cost: the pooled 95% CI for retention is 90.9 to 111.5%, admitting up to 9.1% loss in the worst case but centering on 100.8% (no net cost). For reactive architectures, safety-check rejections drop by 89% and token cost by 85% while completion change is negligible (Cohen's |d| < 0.01). We introduce Bounded Autonomy, a framework that constrains AI agent autonomy along four coordinated dimensions (tool calls, cumulative process perturbation, simulation timesteps, and checkpoint intervals), all calibrated from a single tightness parameter derived from each scenario's estimated optimal action count. Pre-execution middleware, implemented as a LangGraph StateGraph, rejects over-budget actions before they reach the process. Four agent architectures (ReAct, Reflexion, Plan-and-Execute, Hybrid) are evaluated under four budget levels across 20 Continuous Stirred-Tank Reactor (CSTR) scenarios in the OpsEnv benchmark. The evaluation totals over 7,100 experiment cells: 1,680 core Tier 1 cells, 2,800 extended-seed cells, 1,260 cross-model cells, and 1,452 supplementary cells (sensitivity, ablation, rollback, and decoupled experiments). Under tight budgets (1.2× optimal), reactive architectures retain completion (Cohen's |d| < 0.01; Bonferroni-corrected p > 0.05; 95% CI for pooled retention: 90.9 to 111.5%) with 7× wall-time reduction for ReAct and 6.7× for Reflexion. Unconstrained agents take ∼5× more actions than necessary, and these excess actions are counterproductive: in the most pronounced case (scenario B04), a ReAct agent improves from 0.041 to 0.950 completion under budget constraints. Conversely, multi-step optimization tasks (e.g., A04 under ReAct) can lose up to 73 percentage points. Cross-model validation with Qwen 2.5 32B and Llama 3.1 8B (1,260 cells across up to 20 scenarios) confirms the directional violation-reduction effect at reduced magnitude (25% vs. 89% for Tier 1). AI-assisted tools were used in the experimental evaluation; all outputs were reviewed and validated by the authors.

title: Benchmark Prediction with Sparse and Unpaired Cached Responses
abstract: Evaluating a generative model on all queries from all available benchmark tasks is prohibitively expensive. As such, models are often evaluated on different subsets of tasks and/or different subsets of queries from a given task. The resulting collection of responses and the corresponding (model, task) score matrix are sparse and unpaired. In this paper, we introduce the Product Kernel Perspective Space (PKPS), a collection of low-dimensional representations of models based on their embedded responses. PKPS generalizes existing methods for representing black-box generative models by comparing responses to similar -- rather than just identical -- queries and is therefore able to utilize sparse and unpaired information. Theoretically, we show that benchmark prediction using PKPS is query-efficient relative to methods that only use information from dense and paired portions of the evaluation data. Empirically, we show that PKPS-based methods outperform baselines on benchmark prediction across two large benchmark suites.

title: MoviEdit: Long-form Multi-Shot Video Editing Made Easy
abstract: Long-form multi-shot video editing requires an intended edit to remain coherent across abrupt changes in scene, viewpoint, and subject appearance, while processing substantially longer visual context than conventional single-shot editors. We introduce MoviEdit, an end-to-end framework for scalable long-form multi-shot video editing that jointly addresses the challenges of data, modeling, and evaluation. To provide cross-shot supervision data at scale, we develop automatic data-generation pipelines spanning synchronized multi-view footage, real-world multi-shot videos, and generated multi-shot content, yielding 87K paired editing videos without manual annotation. Architecturally, MoviEdit employs a cascaded bidirectional-autoregressive design: a lightweight bidirectional stage first establishes a globally coherent editing draft over a spatiotemporally compressed representation, which is then autoregressively propagated and refined over the full video. We further introduce MoviEdit-Bench, a dedicated benchmark for systematic evaluation of long-form multi-shot video editing. Extensive experiments show that MoviEdit substantially outperforms existing open-source models and performs on par with industry frontier models across text-guided and image-guided editing. Visit our project page for complete results and to access the benchmark: https://multi-shot-edit.github.io/

title: TaoMate-FVSR:Audio-Guided Facial Video Restoration
abstract: AI-generated videos often depict people within detailed scenes while leaving their small facial regions poorly resolved. Visual super-resolution can sharpen these regions without resolving whether the recovered lips and teeth agree with the spoken audio. We present an audio-guided facial video restoration framework that addresses this ambiguity within a reference-guided video flow model. Source--noise mixing initializes reconstruction from a partially preserved observation, and structured reference injection separates appearance anchors from continuous motion context. Training combines restoration of degraded images and videos with correction of degraded dubbed sources under target audio. Appearance and synchronization supervision allow the model to recover facial detail and support visual dubbing when the audio is replaced. On talking-head restoration benchmarks, our method achieves the best paired perceptual similarity and synchronization scores among the compared restoration methods. Component comparisons examine audio conditioning, the reconstruction formulation, and reference injection. Native AIGC examples further illustrate the recovery of lip contours, dental structure, and surrounding facial texture in scene-level footage. injection. title: Lightweight Edge AI Agent for Real-Time Anomaly Detection in Distributed Acoustic Sensing
abstract: Abstract Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) systems generate large volumes of spatiotemporal data that challenge conventional cloud-centric monitoring architectures. Transmitting continuous DAS telemetry for centralized analysis introduces bandwidth, latency, and operational constraints, particularly in remote energy infrastructure environments. This paper presents a lightweight unsupervised edge AI agent for real-time anomaly detection operating on DAS measurements and derived multi-domain feature streams. The proposed framework integrates anomaly scoring, spatiotemporal clustering, trajectory-coherence validation, event severity assessment, autonomous action generation, online memory adaptation, and safety-aware state management within a unified edge-deployable architecture. An agentic processing loop performs perception, anomaly evaluation, event validation, action selection, learning, and safety monitoring while maintaining bounded computational requirements suitable for continuous field deployment. Coherent anomaly events are identified using spatial and temporal consistency criteria, enabling suppression of isolated artifacts and transient noise while preserving operationally meaningful patterns. Detected events are transformed into compact event-centric payloads containing severity, temporal extent, spatial extent, and decision metadata, substantially reducing communication requirements relative to raw data transmission. The framework further incorporates operational trust mechanisms including signed agent manifests, execution-path control, runtime watchdog monitoring, and fail-safe operating modes to support secure and reliable deployment in industrial environments. The framework was evaluated using synthetic datasets and real DAS datasets from field applications, including injection monitoring and microseismic event detection. Results demonstrate effective detection and prioritization of coherent spatiotemporal events without requiring labeled training data. Event-centric reporting reduced communication requirements by 94.36% while processing 1500 DAS channels with a peak memory footprint of 4.83 MB and an average latency below 1 s. The measured performance supports real-time edge deployment without dedicated accelerator hardware. The proposed framework enables scalable, explainable, and communication-efficient DAS monitoring by bringing intelligent event detection, validation, and decision support directly to the network edge.

title: Efficient Closure Learning in Dynamical Systems: A Comparison of Data-Assimilated and Embedded Approaches
abstract: Increased computing power has transformed computational science and improved predictive capabilities for complex systems, but many phenomena still exceed current simulation capabilities or require rapid evaluations for fast design iterations. Closure models address this challenge by approximating unresolved effects in reduced or incomplete dynamical systems. Data-driven closures offer a flexible mechanism for improving model accuracy and applicability, but approaches that embed the closure within a computational model for construction and training phases can be computationally expensive and cause numerical instabilities in the computational model during training. To avoid the challenges posed by embedded approaches, staged approaches to closure-model learning have been developed. The first stage uses data assimilation to infer state and closure trajectories from observations. The second stage trains a machine learning closure model offline using the assimilated data, thereby avoiding repeated simulator calls during training. In this work, we investigate the cost and accuracy tradeoffs between embedded and staged data-driven closure modeling approaches for a synthetic epidemiological SIQR model with a nonlinear state-dependent quarantine closure. The results illustrate a practical accuracy-efficiency trade-off: for this exemplar, embedded training provides the strongest average accuracy, while the staged approach yields comparable qualitative behavior with a moderate increase in error, substantially fewer model evaluations, and improved optimization robustness.

title: 3L-D: A Low-Light Level Dataset from a Sensor-Agnostic, Alignment-Preserving Acquisition Framework
abstract: Supervised low-light image and video enhancement has achieved remarkable progress, yet current models remain fundamentally constrained by the limitations of existing datasets. Prevailing methods typically rely on uncontrolled ambient captures, camera parameter manipulation (e.g., exposure or ISO adjustments), or neutral density filters, failing to replicate authentic night-sky near-infrared spectral content and genuine low-photon noise distributions. Furthermore, capturing dynamic paired sequences without introducing warping artifacts or sensor-specific biases remains an open challenge. In this paper, we introduce 3L-Dataset, a physically calibrated low-light image and video dataset generated using a modular, sensor-agnostic acquisition framework. Our test bench faithfully reproduces the standardized Midavaine night level scale from Level 1 (full moon, approximately 1000 mlx) down to Level 5 (overcast moonless night, approximately 0.1 mlx), spanning the visible to near-infrared spectrum across diverse realistic environments, including countryside, forest, urban, and desert scale models. Using high-precision programmable mechanical actuation, our acquisition framework guarantees sub-pixel spatial alignment across synchronized sextuplets, each composed of one reference image and five corresponding images acquired at the five standardized night levels, without post-processing image warping. We evaluate multiple representative deep learning baselines across varying night levels, revealing critical trade-offs between reconstruction fidelity, perceptual quality, and inference latency under severe photon starvation. The modular acquisition framework can be adapted to different cameras, optical systems, sensor technologies, and resolutions, enabling the dataset to be continuously expanded.

title: Retrieval-Assisted Scalar Grounding for Natural-Language Optimization: A Diagnostic Study
abstract: Abstract Retrieval and structural checks can make natural-language optimization outputs appear usable even when numerical grounding—assigning textual quantities to model parameters—is incomplete. We examine this diagnostic gap through three questions: fixed-catalog schema identification, the validity of coverage/type readiness as a numerical check, and the mechanisms underlying grounding outcomes. On 331 queries from NLP4LP, a benchmark for natural-language linear and mixed-integer linear programming, and 335 schema documents, term frequency–inverse document frequency retrieval and a pretrained dense encoder identify the target schema for 301 and 313 queries. Lexical grounding with multiplicative-word extraction passes coverage/type readiness on 265 queries, but only seven meet the complete stored-reference scalar-tolerance criterion: 2.64% of ready outputs. A mutually exclusive residual partition distinguishes retrieval, coverage, type, and numerical failures. Six grounding procedures under fixed retrieval yield between seven and 46 complete successes, with candidates, scoring, abstention, and decoding changing together. A separate 49-query assignment study with fixed candidates and scores improves exact slot counts without increasing the five whole-instance tolerance successes, limiting attribution to search. The methodological contribution is joint reporting of retrieval, readiness, and complete scalar agreement with explicit assistance, denominators, and evidence boundaries. Reference-derived inventories and benchmark exposure restrict the findings to assisted grounding. Supplementary relationship judgments and author contrasts assisted by artificial intelligence illustrate semantic limits without establishing accuracy. A versioned public release supports saved-record reanalysis; missing historical predictions and restricted originals prevent full experimental reproduction.

title: VerdictAD: Few-Shot Anomaly Detection via Decision-Guided Refinement
abstract: Detecting defects in real-world industrial inspection often requires learning from only a few normal images per category. Recent few-shot anomaly detection methods have achieved strong performance by measuring feature differences between query images and normal references. However, visual differences do not always indicate genuine defects, as normal appearance variations can also produce high anomaly scores. Conversely, structural or logical anomalies may not produce strong local feature differences, making them difficult to detect. To address this limitation, we introduce VerdictAD, a training-free framework that refines existing anomaly detectors through visual decisions. Rather than replacing existing detectors, VerdictAD adopts a typed decision model to assess the query image and its local regions against a few normal references. By directly producing structured decision probabilities without text generation, the model provides complementary evidence for refining anomaly responses at different spatial scales. Building on this capability, we introduce two modules: Global Verdict Refinement (GVR) uses image-level decisions to refine the overall anomaly score, while Local Verdict Refinement (LVR) aggregates regional decisions to refine the anomaly map. Combined with a simple DINOv2-based detector, VerdictAD achieves competitive performance in one-shot and few-shot anomaly detection. More importantly, as a plug-and-play framework, it consistently improves existing anomaly detectors across MVTec AD, VisA, and MVTec LOCO AD, achieving strong results across one-shot and few-shot settings. Our code and experimental logs are publicly available at https://github.com/sgstq0811/VerdictAD-Jev-AD.

title: SeMo3D: Unifying 3D Generation, Editing, and Completion via Selective Modeling
abstract: 3D generation, editing, and completion are typically treated as regenerating the complete 3D asset under task-specific constraints, even when only a local region needs modification. This leads to task isolation, inconsistency in content that should remain unchanged, and dependence on task-specific paired data. We address these issues with a key observation: the three tasks all synthesize a designated region while keeping the rest intact---the full region for generation, the target region for editing, and the missing region for completion. We term this paradigm Selective Modeling and build SeMo3D upon it; it naturally unifies the three tasks, preserves unchanged content by construction, and enables training without paired editing or completion data, since any 3D asset can be partitioned into a selected region and its context. For training, we propose region-selective denoising, which randomly selects regions of varying sizes on standard 3D assets and applies noise and loss only to them, jointly learning all three tasks. For architecture, we propose Omni3DiT, a multi-condition 3D diffusion transformer that distinguishes regions to create from those to retain and fuses image, text, and point guidance for fine-grained control. Experiments across three benchmarks show SeMo3D surpasses state-of-the-art methods on all tasks, delivering multimodal controllability in generation and strong consistency and accuracy in editing and completion. SeMo3D further serves as a unified modeling tool for agents, enabling efficient 3D creation through natural-language interaction. Project page: https://xiaokunsun.github.io/SeMo3D.github.io/.

title: EO-Jev: Decision Model for Earth Observation
abstract: Earth observation (EO) workflows require selecting among known outcomes, estimating confidence, and processing large volumes of imagery. Generative vision-language models can address these tasks, but autoregressive decoding is computationally costly and their confidence estimates are unreliable. Decision models offer an alternative, returning probabilities over candidate answers in a single forward pass. However, their accuracy, calibration, and transfer across EO tasks remain insufficiently understood. We investigate these properties through a diagnostic study of d3-flash (8.4B parameters) across 30 settings from 23 public EO benchmarks. We find that compositional reasoning transfers well and calibration improves over its Qwen3.5-9B backbone on 24 settings, while counting, change quantification, damage grading, and absent-object recognition remain challenging. To address these limitations, we adapt d3-flash through low-rank fine-tuning on public EO training splits, producing EO-Jev. EO-Jev improves significantly over d3-flash on 26 of 30 settings and matches or exceeds specialist references on 20 of 28. It also achieves an average gain of 8.0 points across 12 held-out settings and lower expected calibration error than specialists on 21 of 28 settings. These improvements come at a modest cost of 1.8 points in general decision performance. Our results demonstrate the potential of adapting general decision models into competitive EO generalists while highlighting persistent challenges in quantitative perception, option-order consistency, and calibration under distribution shift.

title: DiabAgent: Toward Agentic Physiological Control
abstract: As pretraining scales, medical language models have advanced rapidly in clinical question answering. Their ability to achieve effective physiological control through sustained intervention still lacks systematic quantitative evaluation. Type 1 diabetes provides a concrete setting: impaired insulin secretion creates dependence on exogenous insulin, with dosing continually adjusted using information about meals, exercise, illness, and glucose measurements. We introduce DiabAgent, a research suite for agentic physiological control comprising the Agentic Physiological Control (APC) framework, the DiabetSim simulator, and the SweetBench benchmark. APC controls glucose through medical-device tools, using ongoing observations to infer individual states, accumulate personal experience, and choose treatment actions. We build DiabetSim to simulate different patients, events, and device conditions for scalable virtual testing and training. Using DiabetSim, we construct SweetBench by instantiating 32 scenario designs as 212 glucose-control tasks. With Claude Opus 5.5 and a fixed decision interval of one hour, APC achieves a COGI of 73.5, compared with 71.2 for the open-source closed-loop baseline OpenAPS. Ablations further show that individual adaptation and contextual information improve glucose control. Combining high-frequency rule-based control with lower-frequency agent decisions shows potential for balancing control performance and computational cost. Our work provides a framework, simulator, and evaluation foundation for agents to participate in human physiological control.

title: MedHEB: Benchmarking Medical Embeddings Across Heterogeneous Clinical Evidence
abstract: Clinical evidence is inherently relational: medical images are interpreted with prior studies, cross-modal examinations, reports, and localized findings, and retrieving relevant evidence is therefore central to clinical interpretation. Recent foundation models increasingly encode these heterogeneous sources into shared embedding spaces, yet existing embedding evaluation often focuses on isolated matches, leaving unclear whether current models retrieve relevant evidence across changes in modality, appearance, and granularity. We introduce MedHEB, a unified benchmark with 107 retrieval tasks from 54 datasets, including both in-distribution and held-out-source evaluation, across three axes: evidence form (2D images, 3D volumes, text), pairing type (image--image, image--text, text--text, and modality-bridging visual matching), and relevance granularity (global, question-conditioned, region-level). Under a single ranking protocol, MedHEB varies clinically relevant evidence definitions to test whether embedding proximity remains meaningful across heterogeneous evidence, including modality-bridging visual retrieval and region-level text-to-region retrieval. Across representative models, performance is uneven across retrieval families: models strong on conventional image--text or text--text retrieval are less reliable on modality-bridging and region-level tasks. Current embedding spaces capture some clinical relationships well but do not yet provide balanced retrieval across heterogeneous evidence. We further provide MedEmb, an MLLM-based reference embedding model trained on the MedHEB ID split, as a reproducible baseline for unified 2D--3D--text medical retrieval. We release MedHEB with preprocessing scripts, evaluation code, access manifests, and MedEmb to support research on clinically meaningful medical embeddings.

title: Every Pixel Is an Option: A System One Model for Medical Ultrasound Biometry
abstract: **Purpose:** Ultrasound biometry is widely used across various clinical applications, including prenatal and cardiac examinations, to obtain quantitative measurements by placing calipers at anatomical landmarks. However, these measurements remain subject to interoperator variability as they rely largely on manual caliper placement. Conventional methods often use specialized prediction heads for different ultrasound tasks, whereas vision-language models offer flexibility through text instructions. However, direct coordinate prediction does not explicitly model spatial likelihood distributions, limiting the representation of localization ambiguity. **Methods:** We propose Kev-Bio, a vision-language model that uses clinical measurement questions to guide ultrasound landmark detection. Inspired by System One decision models, Kev-Bio uses decision representations of the language model to generate queries for each caliper endpoint. These queries are matched against shared dense ultrasound features to produce spatial probability maps, from which landmark coordinates and clinical measurements are derived. The model is trained end-to-end using both landmark localization and clinical measurement losses. **Results:** On the nine-view FU/GU Biometry 2026 dataset, Kev-Bio achieves a mean radial error (MRE) of 22.50 pixels and a clinical measurement mean absolute error (MAE) of 15.38, outperforming the compared baselines in overall performance. **Conclusion:** These results demonstrate the effectiveness of Kev-Bio for ultrasound landmark detection and clinical measurement across different anatomical views. Our code and models are available at https://github.com/moeinheidari7829/Kev-Bio.
